headline: Two bids to clean out and restore the public access building: $58,000 for removal, $93,000 with restoration.
summary: Work would go in steps, starting with the rooms and the studio. About $40,000 in equipment money could be used, but more money would still need Council or Finance Committee approval. City leadership would make the final call, with a goal of taking it to Council in December. Separately, a proposal to swap government and public access channels was postponed.
decisions: Postponed the proposal to switch government and public access programming between Channel 3 and Channel 85.
discussion: Studio building repairs: Two bids were reported, $58,000 for removal only and $93,000 with restoration. Members leaned toward doing the work in steps and discussed whether equipment money could cover part of it.

Cable franchise renegotiation: Members discussed reopening the franchise agreement, and Bill August was contacted about the process. Public input was suggested before any approach to the cable company.

Channel 3 and Channel 85: Members argued over moving government meetings to Channel 85 and keeping public access on Channel 3. Some said Channel 3 is where people look for city meetings, while others said the split would separate the content.
Rodent problem at the studio: A pest control contract had lapsed for years. A barrier under the building was discussed as a first step.
Studio carpet and acoustics: Members discussed replacing the carpet and keeping one wall for sound. Some said room sound would matter more than the look of the space.

decision_evidence.quote: So can we punt on this matter of second? Yes. Yeah.

decision_titles: Switching government and public access channels, 3 and 85

problems.what: tabled, but the decision or the minutes don't say so
